scope: Dollart/Ems to 1914 Danish border on the North Sea mainland coast

comparison.method: historical vertices to nearest canonical-current DEU boundary segment; approximate WGS84 local-distance diagnostic
comparison.warning: The current DEU boundary cannot be used north of the post-1920 German-Danish border and is only a geometric comparison elsewhere, not historical evidence.

sectors.name: cuxhaven-elbe-south-to-hamburg
sectors.note: The national polygon follows the Elbe indentation; historical estuary-bank mapping controls this sector.

sectors.name: husum-1914-danish-border
sectors.note: Modern DEU ceases at the post-1920 border; current-country geometry is not a usable coastline reference here.

canonicalCurrentGeometryConclusion.reason: Natural Earth 10m is too generalized to supply replacement coastline geometry. At the Harle historical endpoint [7.8163122013,53.7114252848], the nearest vertex on the current DEU mainland ring is about 8.97 km away even though point-to-segment distance is small; the apparent agreement is caused by long generalized segments.
canonicalCurrentGeometryConclusion.use: diagnostic comparison only; never substitute current Natural Earth vertices/segments for the 1914 coastline

primary1914.title: Historisch-statistische Grundkarte des Deutschen Reiches: Gemeindegrenzen nach dem Stande des Jahres 1914

knownChangeMasks.name: Wilhelmshaven/Innenjade Groden
knownChangeMasks.evidence: Major modern reclamations began with Heppenser Groden 1936-1938, followed by Rüstersieler Groden 1960-1963, Voslapper Groden 1971-1974 and JadeWeserPort 2008-2012.

knownChangeMasks.name: Unterweser/Außenweser
knownChangeMasks.evidence: The 7 m Lower Weser deepening ran 1913-1916, so 1914 lies inside an active engineering phase.

knownChangeMasks.name: North Friesland post-1914 reclamation
knownChangeMasks.evidence: Sönke-Nissen-Koog construction started in 1924; it must not appear in the 1914 coastline.
